Cautiously positive. The FOMC notes that activity and employment “have turned up” while pandemic-hit sectors remain weak and inflation is below 2%, and it reinforces an accommodative stance with the policy rate at 0–0.25% and ongoing Treasury/MBS purchases. In a New Keynesian framework (Clarida–Galí–Gertler), credible forward guidance to keep rates low until maximum employment and inflation moderately exceed 2% reduces expected real rates and supports demand (Woodford), while average-inflation/forecast targeting helps anchor expectations near 2% (Svensson). Large-scale asset purchases should compress term premia and flatten the yield curve (Cochrane–Piazzesi), and the credit channel literature (Bernanke–Gertler) implies improved credit flow to households and firms. A Taylor-rule perspective also justifies highly accommodative policy given slack and subtarget inflation. Offsetting this, the statement underscores virus-related downside risks. Overall tone: mildly positive.
